intended_object: For a commutative ring R, the canonical ring homomorphism from the semiring of isomorphism classes of finitely generated projective R-modules (with ⊕ as addition and ⊗ as multiplication) to its group completion K₀(R), which carries the tensor-product ring structure (Weibel, K-book II.2). The docstring and module docs state this.
explanation:
K0 R is defined as `Algebra.GrothendieckAddGroup (ProjectiveClass R)`. The definition is the library's generic canonical ring map `A →+* GrothendieckAddGroup A`, built from `of` with `map_one` and `map_mul`, applied to A = ProjectiveClass R. Its underlying additive map is the completion map `ofClass` (shown by `rfl`), and it sends [M] to the K₀ generator of M. That is the standard map from the semiring of iso classes to K₀(R).

The classes are right Rᵐᵒᵖ-modules. Since R is commutative, Rᵐᵒᵖ ≅ R, so these are ordinary R-modules. Commutativity of R is also what makes ⊗ a semiring structure, so asking for `CommRing` is the natural setting and not an over-restriction.

Mathlib has `Algebra.GrothendieckAddGroup` only as an additive group. It has no ring structure on it and no K₀ of a ring, so it has no counterpart for this map.
